sanskrit: yat tenoktaṃ duruktaṃ tat tadānīṃ; hṛdi sthitaṃ tasya suduḥkham āsīt gṛhaṃ gatvā mātaraṃ rodamānaḥ; papracchedaṃ kva nu tāto mameti
english: The harsh words spoken by him then lodged in his heart as profound sorrow. Going home, weeping, he asked his mother: 'Where indeed is my father?'

sanskrit: tataḥ sujātā paramārtarūpā; śāpād bhītā sarvam evācacakṣe tad vai tattvaṃ sarvam ājñāya mātur; ity abravīc chvetaketuṃ sa vipraḥ
english: Then Sujātā, overwhelmed with grief and afraid of the curse, revealed everything in full. Knowing the entire truth from his mother, that brahmin then addressed Śvetaketu.

sanskrit: gacchāva yajñaṃ janakasya rājño; bahvāścaryaḥ śrūyate tasya yajñaḥ śroṣyāvo 'tra brāhmaṇānāṃ vivādam; annaṃ cāgryaṃ tatra bhokṣyāvahe ca vicakṣaṇatvaṃ ca bhaviṣyate nau; śivaś ca saumyaś ca hi brahmaghoṣaḥ
english: 'Let us go to the sacrifice of King Janaka — his sacrifice is said to be full of wonders. We shall listen to the debates among the brahmins there and partake of the finest food; we shall gain discernment, for the sound of the Veda there is auspicious and gentle.'

sanskrit: tau jagmatur mātulabhāgineyau; yajñaṃ samṛddhaṃ janakasya rājñaḥ aṣṭāvakraḥ pathi rājñā sametya; utsāryamāṇo vākyam idaṃ jagāda
english: So those two — uncle and nephew — went to the opulent sacrifice of King Janaka. Aṣṭāvakra, encountering the king on the road and being turned away, spoke these words.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca andhasya panthā badhirasya panthāḥ; striyaḥ panthā vaivadhikasya panthāḥ rājñaḥ panthā brāhmaṇenāsametya; sametya tu brāhmaṇasyaiva panthāḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'The road belongs to the blind; the road belongs to the deaf; the road belongs to women; the road belongs to the burden-carrier. A king's road yields when a brahmin is present — when a brahmin is met, the road is the brahmin's alone.'

sanskrit: rājovāca panthā ayaṃ te 'dya mayā nisṛṣṭo; yenecchase tena kāmaṃ vrajasva na pāvako vidyate vai laghīyān; indro 'pi nityaṃ namate brāhmaṇānām
english: The king said: 'This road is granted to you by me today — go as you wish, freely. There is no purer light than fire, and even Indra himself perpetually bows to brahmins.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca yajñaṃ draṣṭuṃ prāptavantau sva tāta; kautūhalaṃ nau balavad vai vivṛddham āvāṃ prāptāv atithī saṃpraveśaṃ; kāṅkṣāvahe dvārapate tavājñām
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'We have come to witness the sacrifice, O lord. Our curiosity has grown very strong. Having arrived as guests, we desire entry — O doorkeeper, we await your command.'

sanskrit: aindradyumner yajñadṛśāv ihāvāṃ; vivakṣū vai janakendraṃ didṛkṣū na vai krodhād vyādhinaivottamena; saṃyojaya dvārapāla kṣaṇena
english: 'We two have come here to see the sacrifice of the son of Indradyumna, and we wish to speak with King Janaka and behold him. Not from anger nor from any great affliction — O doorkeeper, announce us in a moment.'

sanskrit: dvārapāla uvāca bandeḥ samādeśakarā vayaṃ sma; nibodha vākyaṃ ca mayeryamāṇam na vai bālāḥ praviśanty atra viprā; vṛddhā vidvāṃsaḥ praviśanti dvijāgryāḥ
english: The doorkeeper said: 'We are the order-bearers of Bandin — hear the words I pronounce: no young brahmins enter here; only the aged and learned, the foremost among the twice-born, may enter.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca yady atra vṛddheṣu kṛtaḥ praveśo; yuktaṃ mama dvārapāla praveṣṭum vayaṃ hi vṛddhāś caritavratāś ca; vedaprabhāvena praveśanārhāḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'If entry here is granted to the aged, then it is fitting, O doorkeeper, that I enter — for we are old, observers of vows, and by the power of the Veda we are worthy of entry.'

sanskrit: śuśrūṣavaś cāpi jitendriyāś ca; jñānāgame cāpi gatāḥ sma niṣṭhām na bāla ity avamantavyam āhur; bālo 'py agnir dahati spṛśyamānaḥ
english: 'We are devoted to learning, have mastered our senses, and have reached perfection in the acquisition of knowledge. One should not be disrespected as a mere child — even fire, though young, burns when touched.'

sanskrit: dvārapāla uvāca sarasvatīm īraya vedajuṣṭām; ekākṣarāṃ bahurūpāṃ virājam aṅgātmānaṃ samavekṣasva bālaṃ; kiṃ ślāghase durlabhā vādasiddhiḥ
english: The doorkeeper said: 'Set in motion Sarasvatī beloved of the Veda — the one syllable, multiform, radiant. Look at yourself, O child, body and soul. Why do you boast? Victory in debate is hard to win.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca na jñāyate kāyavṛddhyā vivṛddhir; yathāṣṭhīlā śālmaleḥ saṃpravṛddhā hrasvo 'lpakāyaḥ phalito vivṛddho; yaś cāphalas tasya na vṛddhabhāvaḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Greatness is not known by bodily growth — just as the knot of the silk-cotton tree grows large yet is hollow. A short man of small body who bears fruit is truly great; one who bears no fruit has no true greatness.'

sanskrit: dvārapāla uvāca vṛddhebhya eveha matiṃ sma bālā; gṛhṇanti kālena bhavanti vṛddhāḥ na hi jñānam alpakālena śakyaṃ; kasmād bālo vṛddha ivāvabhāṣase
english: The doorkeeper said: 'Children acquire wisdom here from the aged, and become old themselves with time. Knowledge cannot truly be won in a short span — why then do you, a child, speak as though you were an elder?'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca na tena sthaviro bhavati yenāsya palitaṃ śiraḥ bālo 'pi yaḥ prajānāti taṃ devāḥ sthaviraṃ viduḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'One does not become an elder merely because one's hair has turned grey. Even a child who truly knows — him the gods consider an elder.'

sanskrit: na hāyanair na palitair na vittena na bandhubhiḥ ṛṣayaś cakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān
english: 'Not by years, not by grey hair, not by wealth, not by kinsmen — the sages established dharma. He who has learned and taught the sacred texts — he is great among us.'

sanskrit: didṛkṣur asmi saṃprāpto bandinaṃ rājasaṃsadi nivedayasva māṃ dvāḥstha rājñe puṣkaramāline
english: 'I have come wishing to see Bandin in the royal assembly. Announce me, O doorkeeper, to the king who wears the lotus garland.'

sanskrit: draṣṭāsy adya vadato dvārapāla; manīṣibhiḥ saha vāde vivṛddhe utāho vāpy uccatāṃ nīcatāṃ vā; tūṣṇīṃ bhūteṣv atha sarveṣu cādya
english: 'You shall see today, O doorkeeper, in debate grown intense among the wise — whether I shall rise high or fall low, or whether all remain silent today.'

sanskrit: dvārapāla uvāca kathaṃ yajñaṃ daśavarṣo viśes tvaṃ; vinītānāṃ viduṣāṃ saṃpraveśyam upāyataḥ prayatiṣye tavāhaṃ; praveśane kuru yatnaṃ yathāvat
english: The doorkeeper said: 'How shall you, ten years old, enter this sacrifice that is the domain of the learned and the humble? I will endeavour by proper means to arrange your entry — make the effort as is fitting.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca bho bho rājañ janakānāṃ variṣṭha; sabhājyas tvaṃ tvayi sarvaṃ samṛddham tvaṃ vā kartā karmaṇāṃ yajñiyānāṃ; yayātir eko nṛpatir vā purastāt
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'O king, O best of the Janaka line — you are worthy of reverence; all prosperity resides in you. You are the performer of sacrificial rites, as once was the sole king Yayāti before you.'

sanskrit: vidvān bandī vedavido nigṛhya; vāde bhagnān apratiśaṅkamānaḥ tvayā nisṛṣṭaiḥ puruṣair āptakṛdbhir; jale sarvān majjayatīti naḥ śrutam
english: 'Bandin the learned, having defeated in debate those who know the Vedas, without hesitation or second thought, causes all those broken ones — dispatched by your trusted men — to be drowned in the water. So we have heard.'

sanskrit: sa tac chrutvā brāhmaṇānāṃ sakāśād; brahmodyaṃ vai kathayitum āgato 'smi kvāsau bandī yāvad enaṃ sametya; nakṣatrāṇīva savitā nāśayāmi
english: 'Hearing that from the brahmins, I have come to engage in Brahmodya debate. Where is that Bandin? Once I meet him, I shall destroy him as the sun destroys the stars.'

sanskrit: rājovāca āśaṃsase bandinaṃ tvaṃ vijetum; avijñātvā vākyabalaṃ parasya vijñātavīryaiḥ śakyam evaṃ pravaktuṃ; dṛṣṭaś cāsau brāhmaṇair vādaśīlaiḥ
english: The king said: 'You hope to defeat Bandin without knowing the power of his speech. Only one who has ascertained the strength of the opponent can speak thus — and he has been tested by brahmins skilled in debate.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca vivādito 'sau na hi mādṛśair hi; siṃhīkṛtas tena vadaty abhītaḥ sametya māṃ nihataḥ śeṣyate 'dya; mārge bhagnaṃ śakaṭam ivābalākṣam
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'He has not been contested by ones like me. He speaks fearlessly, made bold as a lion. When he meets me he shall be struck down today, lying shattered on the road like a broken cart that weak-eyed oxen could not draw.'

sanskrit: rājovāca ṣaṇṇābher dvādaśākṣasya caturviṃśatiparvaṇaḥ yas triṣaṣṭiśatārasya vedārthaṃ sa paraḥ kaviḥ
english: The king said: 'He who knows the meaning of the Veda — the wheel with six hubs, twelve spokes, twenty-four segments, and three hundred and sixty-three spokes — he is the supreme sage.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca caturviṃśatiparva tvāṃ ṣaṇṇābhi dvādaśapradhi tat triṣaṣṭiśatāraṃ vai cakraṃ pātu sadāgati
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'May that wheel of twenty-four segments, six hubs, twelve rims, three hundred and sixty-three spokes, ever-moving, protect you.'

sanskrit: rājovāca vaḍave iva saṃyukte śyenapāte divaukasām kas tayor garbham ādhatte garbhaṃ suṣuvatuś ca kam
english: The king said: 'In the union of two like mares, in the flight of the eagle among the celestials — who bears the embryo of those two, and what embryo did they bring forth?'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca mā sma te te gṛhe rājañ śātravāṇām api dhruvam vātasārathir ādhatte garbhaṃ suṣuvatuś ca tam
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'May this never occur in your house, O king — not even in the houses of your enemies is it certain. Vāta, whose charioteer is wind, bears that embryo, and they brought it forth.'

sanskrit: rājovāca kiṃ svit suptaṃ na nimiṣati kiṃ svij jātaṃ na copati kasya svid dhṛdayaṃ nāsti kiṃ svid vegena vardhate
english: The king said: 'What sleeps without blinking? What, once born, does not stir? Whose heart does not exist? What grows swiftly?'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca matsyaḥ supto na nimiṣaty aṇḍaṃ jātaṃ na copati aśmano hṛdayaṃ nāsti nadī vegena vardhate
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'A fish sleeps without blinking; an egg, once born, does not stir; a stone has no heart; a river grows swiftly.'

sanskrit: rājovāca na tvā manye mānuṣaṃ devasattvaṃ; na tvaṃ bālaḥ sthaviras tvaṃ mato me na te tulyo vidyate vākpralāpe; tasmād dvāraṃ vitarāmy eṣa bandī
english: The king said: 'I do not regard you as human — yours is the nature of a divine being. You are not a child; in my estimation you are an elder. There is none equal to you in the flow of speech. Therefore I grant you the door — and there is Bandin.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca atrograsenasamiteṣu rājan; samāgateṣv apratimeṣu rājasu na vai vivitsāntaram asti vādināṃ; mahājale haṃsaninādinām iva
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'O king, here where the assembly of Ugrasena has convened, where peerless kings have gathered — among these debaters there is no difference in the desire to know, like swans calling in a great lake.'

sanskrit: na me 'dya vakṣyasy ativādimānin; glahaṃ prapannaḥ saritām ivāgamaḥ hutāśanasyeva samiddhatejasaḥ; sthiro bhavasveha mamādya bandin
english: 'You will not speak against me today, O you who pride yourself on excessive speech. Like the arrival of rivers, like the blazing brilliance of fire kindled — be firm here against me today, O Bandin.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca vyāghraṃ śayānaṃ prati mā prabodhaya; āśīviṣaṃ sṛkkiṇī lelihānam padāhatasyeva śiro 'bhihatya; nādaṣṭo vai mokṣyase tan nibodha
english: Bandin said: 'Do not rouse a sleeping tiger. Do not place your head where the venomous snake is flicking its tongue in rage — one who has stepped on it cannot escape unbitten. Understand this.'

sanskrit: yo vai darpāt saṃhananopapannaḥ; sudurbalaḥ parvatam āvihanti tasyaiva pāṇiḥ sanakho viśīryate; na caiva śailasya hi dṛśyate vraṇaḥ
english: 'One who, puffed up with pride and however strong in frame, yet utterly feeble in true power, strikes against a mountain — only his own hand with its nails shatters; no wound at all is seen on the rock.'

sanskrit: sarve rājño maithilasya mainākasyeva parvatāḥ nikṛṣṭabhūtā rājāno vatsā anaduho yathā
english: 'All kings stand like mere mountains before King Mithilā — made low, diminished, like calves before a draught-ox.'

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca aṣṭāvakraḥ samitau garjamāno; jātakrodho bandinam āha rājan ukte vākye cottaraṃ me bravīhi; vākyasya cāpy uttaraṃ te bravīmi
english: Lomaśa said: 'Aṣṭāvakra, roaring in the assembly, filled with anger, addressed Bandin, O king: "To the word I have spoken, give me your reply — and I too shall give you the reply to your word."'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca eka evāgnir bahudhā samidhyate; ekaḥ sūryaḥ sarvam idaṃ prabhāsate eko vīro devarājo nihantā; yamaḥ pitṝṇām īśvaraś caika eva
english: Bandin said: 'Fire is one, kindled in many forms; the sun is one, illuminating all this world; the hero, the destroyer, the king of gods, is one; Yama, the lord of the ancestors, is one alone.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca dvāv indrāgnī carato vai sakhāyau; dvau devarṣī nāradaḥ parvataś ca dvāv aśvinau dve ca rathasya cakre; bhāryāpatī dvau vihitau vidhātrā
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Indra and Agni, two companions, move together; two divine sages — Nārada and Parvata; two Aśvins; two wheels of a chariot; husband and wife — these two are ordained by the Creator.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca triḥ sūyate karmaṇā vai prajeyaṃ; trayo yuktā vājapeyaṃ vahanti adhvaryavas triṣavaṇāni tanvate; trayo lokās trīṇi jyotīṃṣi cāhuḥ
english: Bandin said: 'Progeny is produced three times through ritual action; three bearers carry the Vājapeya sacrifice; the Adhvaryus perform the three pressings; there are three worlds, and they speak of three lights.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca catuṣṭayaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ niketaṃ; catvāro yuktā yajñam imaṃ vahanti diśaś catasraś caturaś ca varṇāś; catuṣpadā gaur api śaśvad uktā
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Fourfold is the abode of the brahmins; four bearers carry this sacrifice; four are the directions; four are the social orders; and the cow too is always called four-footed.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca pañcāgnayaḥ pañcapadā ca paṅktir; yajñāḥ pañcaivāpy atha pañcendriyāṇi dṛṣṭā vede pañcacūḍāś ca pañca; loke khyātaṃ pañcanadaṃ ca puṇyam
english: Bandin said: 'Five are the sacred fires; the Paṅkti metre has five feet; five are the sacrifices; five the sense organs as seen in the Veda; and five are the five-crested ones — and the holy Pañcanada is famous in the world.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca ṣaḍādhāne dakṣiṇām āhur eke; ṣaḍ eveme ṛtavaḥ kālacakram ṣaḍ indriyāṇy uta ṣaṭ kṛttikāś ca; ṣaṭ sādyaskāḥ sarvavedeṣu dṛṣṭāḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Some say the sacrificial fee is sixfold at the fire installation; six are the seasons that make the wheel of time; six are the senses; six too are the Kṛttikā stars; and the six Sādyaskā rites are seen across all the Vedas.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca sapta grāmyāḥ paśavaḥ sapta vanyāḥ; sapta chandāṃsi kratum ekaṃ vahanti saptarṣayaḥ sapta cāpy arhaṇāni; saptatantrī prathitā caiva vīṇā
english: Bandin said: 'Seven are the domestic animals; seven the wild ones; seven metres carry the one sacrifice; seven are the seers; seven too are the forms of worship; and the seven-stringed lute is renowned.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca aṣṭau śāṇāḥ śatamānaṃ vahanti; tathāṣṭapādaḥ śarabhaḥ siṃhaghātī aṣṭau vasūñ śuśruma devatāsu; yūpaś cāṣṭāsrir vihitaḥ sarvayajñaḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Eight Śāṇas make a Śatamāna; the eight-legged Śarabha slays the lion; we have heard eight Vasus among the gods; and the sacrificial post is appointed with eight corners in all sacrifices.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca navaivoktāḥ sāmidhenyaḥ pitṝṇāṃ; tathā prāhur navayogaṃ viṣargam navākṣarā bṛhatī saṃpradiṣṭā; navayogo gaṇanām eti śaśvat
english: Bandin said: 'The Sāmidhenī hymns for the ancestors are declared to be nine; nine too they call the Navayoga of emission; the Bṛhatī metre is prescribed as having nine syllables; and the Navayoga count proceeds for ever.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca daśā daśoktāḥ puruṣasya loke; sahasram āhur daśa pūrṇaṃ śatāni daśaiva māsān bibhrati garbhavatyo; daśerakā daśa dāśā daśārṇāḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Ten Daśās are counted for a man in the world; a thousand is said to be ten complete hundreds; pregnant women carry their burden for ten months; and there are the Daśeraka, the ten Dāśā, and the Daśārṇa.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca ekādaśaikādaśinaḥ paśūnām; ekādaśaivātra bhavanti yūpāḥ ekādaśa prāṇabhṛtāṃ vikārā; ekādaśoktā divi deveṣu rudrāḥ
english: Bandin said: 'Eleven are the Ekādaśina sets of animals; eleven are the sacrificial posts here; eleven are the transformations of beings that breathe; and eleven Rudras are declared among the gods in heaven.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca saṃvatsaraṃ dvādaśa māsam āhur; jagatyāḥ pādo dvādaśaivākṣarāṇi dvādaśāhaḥ prākṛto yajña ukto; dvādaśādityān kathayantīha viprāḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'A year is said to have twelve months; the Jagatī foot has exactly twelve syllables; the twelve-day rite is declared the natural sacrifice; and the brahmins here speak of twelve Ādityas.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca trayodaśī tithir uktā mahogrā; trayodaśadvīpavatī mahī ca
english: Bandin said: 'The thirteenth lunar day is declared most terrible and fierce; and the earth too has thirteen island-continents.'

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca etāvad uktvā virarāma bandī; ślokasyārdhaṃ vyājahārāṣṭavakraḥ trayodaśāhāni sasāra keśī; trayodaśādīny aticchandāṃsi cāhuḥ
english: Lomaśa said: 'Having spoken that much, Bandin fell silent — only half a verse. Aṣṭāvakra then spoke the other half: "Keśin traversed thirteen days; and those beginning with thirteen are called the Atichandas metres."'

sanskrit: tato mahān udatiṣṭhan ninādas; tūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ sūtaputraṃ niśamya adhomukhaṃ dhyānaparaṃ tadānīm; aṣṭāvakraṃ cāpy udīryantam eva
english: Then a great roar arose, seeing Bandin the sūta's son fallen silent, head bowed, absorbed in thought — and Aṣṭāvakra still rising in triumph.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā saṃkule vartamāne; sphīte yajñe janakasyātha rājñaḥ aṣṭāvakraṃ pūjayanto 'bhyupeyur; viprāḥ sarve prāñjalayaḥ pratītāḥ
english: As that tumult prevailed at the opulent sacrifice of King Janaka, all the brahmins, with hands folded in reverence and hearts delighted, came forward to honour Aṣṭāvakra.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca anena vai brāhmaṇāḥ śuśruvāṃso; vāde jitvā salile majjitāḥ kila tān eva dharmān ayam adya bandī; prāpnotu gṛhyāpsu nimajjayainam
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'O brahmins — those who were defeated in debate by this man and reportedly drowned in the water — let this Bandin now receive those same laws today; seize him and plunge him into the water.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca ahaṃ putro varuṇasyota rājñas; tatrāsa satraṃ dvādaśavārṣikaṃ vai satreṇa te janaka tulyakālaṃ; tadarthaṃ te prahitā me dvijāgryāḥ
english: Bandin said: 'I am the son of Varuṇa the king. There was a twelve-year satra sacrifice of his — contemporaneous in time with your sacrifice, O Janaka. For its purpose those foremost twice-born were sent there by me.'

sanskrit: ete sarve varuṇasyota yajñaṃ; draṣṭuṃ gatā iha āyānti bhūyaḥ aṣṭāvakraṃ pūjaye pūjanīyaṃ; yasya hetor janitāraṃ sameṣye
english: 'All of these have gone to witness Varuṇa's sacrifice and will come back here again. I honour the honourable Aṣṭāvakra — for whose sake I shall now go to meet his father.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca viprāḥ samudrāmbhasi majjitās te; vācā jitā medhayā āvidānāḥ tāṃ medhayā vācam athojjahāra; yathā vācam avacinvanti santaḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'Those brahmins were plunged into the ocean's waters — defeated by speech, overwhelmed by intellect. Yet with that very intellect speech was then restored, just as the noble gather speech from speech.'

sanskrit: agnir dahañ jātavedāḥ satāṃ gṛhān; visarjayaṃs tejasā na sma dhākṣīt bāleṣu putreṣu kṛpaṇaṃ vadatsu; tathā vācam avacinvanti santaḥ
english: 'Agni, Jātavedas, burning and releasing the homes of the virtuous with his radiance, did not scorch them even as their young children cried out piteously — thus do the noble gather speech from speech.'

sanskrit: śleṣmātakī kṣīṇavarcāḥ śṛṇoṣi; utāho tvāṃ stutayo mādayanti hastīva tvaṃ janaka vitudyamāno; na māmikāṃ vācam imāṃ śṛṇoṣi
english: 'O Janaka, like a śleṣmātaka tree of diminished lustre — do you hear, or do praises merely intoxicate you? Like an elephant being goaded, you do not hear this my speech.'

sanskrit: janaka uvāca śṛṇomi vācaṃ tava divyarūpām; amānuṣīṃ divyarūpo 'si sākṣāt ajaiṣīr yad bandinaṃ tvaṃ vivāde; nisṛṣṭa eṣa tava kāmo 'dya bandī
english: Janaka said: 'I do hear your speech, divine in nature, superhuman — you are a divine form manifest. That you have conquered Bandin in debate — this your wish is granted; Bandin is released to you today.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca nānena jīvatā kaś cid artho me bandinā nṛpa pitā yady asya varuṇo majjayainaṃ jalāśaye
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: 'I have no use for this Bandin as long as he lives, O king. If his father is Varuṇa, then let him plunge him into the watery deep.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca ahaṃ putro varuṇasyota rājño; na me bhayaṃ salile majjitasya imaṃ muhūrtaṃ pitaraṃ drakṣyate 'yam; aṣṭāvakraś ciranaṣṭaṃ kahoḍam
english: Bandin said: 'I am the son of Varuṇa the king — I have no fear of being plunged into the water. In this very moment Aṣṭāvakra shall see his long-lost father Kahoḍa.'

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tatas te pūjitā viprā varuṇena mahātmanā udatiṣṭhanta te sarve janakasya samīpataḥ
english: Lomaśa said: 'Then those brahmins, honoured by the great-souled Varuṇa, all rose up in the presence of Janaka.'

sanskrit: kahoḍa uvāca ityartham icchanti sutāñ janā janaka karmaṇā yad ahaṃ nāśakaṃ kartuṃ tat putraḥ kṛtavān mama
english: Kahoḍa said: 'It is for this purpose that people desire sons, O Janaka — through his deeds, that which I was unable to do, my son has accomplished.'

sanskrit: utābalasya balavān uta bālasya paṇḍitaḥ uta vāviduṣo vidvān putro janaka jāyate
english: 'A powerful son is born of one who is weak, O Janaka; a learned son of one who is ignorant; and a knowledgeable son of one who does not know.'

sanskrit: bandy uvāca śitena te paraśunā svayam evāntako nṛpa śirāṃsy apāharatv ājau ripūṇāṃ bhadram astu te
english: Bandin said: 'May Death himself, with your sharpened axe, lop off the heads of your enemies in battle, O king. May all be well with you.'

sanskrit: mahad ukthyaṃ gīyate sāma cāgryaṃ; samyak somaḥ pīyate cātra satre śucīn bhāgān pratijagṛhuś ca hṛṣṭāḥ; sākṣād devā janakasyeha yajñe
english: 'The great Ukthya is sung and the foremost Sāman; the Soma is duly pressed and drunk at this satra. With joy the gods themselves in person accepted their pure shares at the sacrifice of Janaka here.'

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca samutthiteṣv atha sarveṣu rājan; vipreṣu teṣv adhikaṃ suprabheṣu anujñāto janakenātha rājñā; viveśa toyaṃ sāgarasyota bandī
english: Lomaśa said: 'Then, O king, when all those brahmins of surpassing radiance had risen, with King Janaka's leave, Bandin entered the waters of the ocean.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakraḥ pitaraṃ pūjayitvā; saṃpūjito brāhmaṇais tair yathāvat pratyājagāmāśramam eva cāgryaṃ; jitvā bandiṃ sahito mātulena
english: Aṣṭāvakra, having honoured his father and been duly honoured in return by those brahmins, came back to the foremost hermitage, having defeated Bandin, together with his maternal uncle.

sanskrit: atra kaunteya sahito bhrātṛbhis tvaṃ; sukhoṣitaḥ saha vipraiḥ pratītaḥ puṇyāny anyāni śucikarmaikabhaktir; mayā sārdhaṃ caritāsy ājamīḍha
english: 'Here, O son of Kuntī, you shall dwell happily together with your brothers, accompanied by the brahmins and with joy. You shall perform other meritorious deeds — pure in action, devoted to one aim — along with me, O scion of Ajamīḍha.'

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca eṣā madhuvilā rājan samaṅgā saṃprakāśate etat kardamilaṃ nāma bharatasyābhiṣecanam
english: Lomaśa said: 'O king, this Madhuvilā — the Samaṅgā river — shines forth here. This is called the Kardamila, the site of Bharata's coronation bath.'

sanskrit: alakṣmyā kila saṃyukto vṛtraṃ hatvā śacīpatiḥ āplutaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ samaṅgāyāṃ vyamucyata
english: 'It is said that the lord of Śacī, afflicted by the sin of killing Vṛtra, bathed here and was freed from all sins in the Samaṅgā.'

sanskrit: etad vinaśanaṃ kukṣau mainākasya nararṣabha aditir yatra putrārthaṃ tadannam apacat purā
english: 'This is the Vinaśana, in the flank of Mount Mainākā, O bull among men — where Aditi once cooked that food for the sake of offspring.'

sanskrit: enaṃ parvatarājānam āruhya puruṣarṣabha ayaśasyām asaṃśabdyām alakṣmīṃ vyapanotsyatha
english: 'Ascending this king of mountains, O bull among men, you shall drive away the ill-reputed, unspeakable inauspiciousness.'

sanskrit: ete kanakhalā rājan ṛṣīṇāṃ dayitā nagāḥ eṣā prakāśate gaṅgā yudhiṣṭhira mahānadī
english: 'These are the Kanakahalā trees, O king, beloved of the seers. And here, O Yudhiṣṭhira, shines forth the great river Gaṅgā.'

sanskrit: sanatkumāro bhagavān atra siddhim agāt parām ājamīḍhāvagāhyaināṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramokṣyase
english: 'The blessed Sanatkumāra attained the highest perfection here. O descendant of Ajamīḍha, plunge into this river and you shall be freed from all sins.'

sanskrit: apāṃ hradaṃ ca puṇyākhyaṃ bhṛgutuṅgaṃ ca parvatam tūṣṇīṃ gaṅgāṃ ca kaunteya sāmātyaḥ samupaspṛśa
english: 'The holy lake called Apāṃhrada, the mountain Bhṛgutuṅga, and the silent Gaṅgā — O son of Kuntī, touch all these along with your ministers.'

sanskrit: āśramaḥ sthūlaśiraso ramaṇīyaḥ prakāśate atra mānaṃ ca kaunteya krodhaṃ caiva vivarjaya
english: 'The charming hermitage of Sthūlaśiras shines forth here. O son of Kuntī, in this place abandon both pride and anger.'

sanskrit: eṣa raibhyāśramaḥ śrīmān pāṇḍaveya prakāśate bhāradvājo yatra kavir yavakrīto vyanaśyata
english: 'This is the glorious hermitage of Raibhya, shining forth, O son of Pāṇḍu — where the learned son of Bharadvāja, Yavakrīta, met his end.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃyukto 'bhavad ṛṣir bharadvājaḥ pratāpavān kimarthaṃ ca yavakrīta ṛṣiputro vyanaśyata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: 'How was the sage Bharadvāja of great power situated? And for what reason did Yavakrīta, son of the sage, perish?'
